goal: Make the intent -> Core Builder repair loop -> frontend publication path real, auditable, and extensible beyond Codex CLI.
acceptance: Every one of the 20 cases has a materialized testdata/<case-id>/ input and explicit browser acceptance contract.
The CLI prompt names intent, goal, flow, expected outcome, exact data paths, writable directories, and acceptance procedure.
A Core Builder run can use native Codex subagents for acceptance, rerun after failures, and only publish after an independent deterministic browser test passes.
The run retains full CLI dialogue and acceptance evidence while repository core files remain unchanged.
The core adapter boundary can accept another harness without changing intent or publication logic.
